page: Microsoft Azure D8ls_v6 is an x86_64 cloud instance operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is equipped with 8 vCPUs originating from 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573B processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. Memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB, resulting in an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not provide local ephemeral storage and includes zero GPU accelerators. All persistent disk I/O depends on attached network storage volumes, for which the instance supports premium storage configurations. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the VM by default.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2178.0, single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 31.36 GB/sec, and high-tier text processing metrics. In contrast, multi-core metrics fall within the middle 50% benchmark tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8357.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14366.13. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 66.69 GB/sec for reads and 45.92 GB/sec for writes. In small-model inference (135M parameters), text generation reached 283.15 tokens per second, but generation speed reduced to 7.37 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration creates a low-memory profile that prioritizes processor cycle efficiency over capacity per core. Because persistent storage relies entirely on external volumes, I/O-intensive workloads must account for network storage latency. The D8ls_v6 is targeted at CPU-bound tasks with moderate RAM requirements, including software compilation pipelines, web application serving, batch data manipulation, and lightweight microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ls_v6 is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573B processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Delivered via Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and 260 MB of L3 cache. The CPU incorporates vector and matrix acceleration extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on external network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile single-core metrics, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2178.0 and 31.36 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core compute, Redis throughput, and memory bandwidth track within the industry average. Given its compact 1:2 memory ratio and high clock speed, the D8ls_v6 is configured for compute-constrained environments, CI/CD compilation, web serving, and CPU-bound microservices.
